# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Titles:** queen of housemothers  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears. She has large, soft blue eyes that shine with unquenchable youth and hopes.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is a sweet, mirthful, and old-fashioned woman who admits to holding comfortable, traditional opinions and wearing old-fashioned clothes. Although she can speak severely or express a low opinion of others, she loves deeply to atone for it. She possesses a proper respect for the clergy and hates visiting. She handles unexpected circumstances with a charming grace and takes life easily.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c19 P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040), [v3 c20 P10](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0010), [v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011), [v3 c37 P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## History

Left alone in a large house after her daughter Elizabeth married and went to the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Jamesina accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport to keep house at Patty's Place for college students Anne, Priscilla, Phil, and Stella. During cold winter nights, she allowed the cats—Rusty, Joseph, and the Sarah-cat—to sleep indoors, taking comfort in the Sarah-cat's purring to soothe her fears about snakes in India. After the students graduated, she remained at Patty's Place to care for the cats, preferring it over opening her own home or visiting. Later, despite her terror of snakes, she traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c20 P10](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0010), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- named Jamesina after her father James who was drowned at sea a month before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- always wanted a yellow silk dress, but her mother and husband refused  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- used to make fun of her beaux in her youth  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
- prayed for her daughter Elizabeth to become a missionary  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- never attended college  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>
- suggested to a beau that he train his ears with a rubber band  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>

## Quotes

> It’s a very old-fashioned way. But I am old-fashioned. My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too. I don’t say they’re any the better of that, mind you. In fact, I daresay they’re a good deal the worse. But they’ve worn nice and easy. New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions. I mean to take it real easy here. I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I’m not going to do it. You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> There’s magic in the words ‘silk’ and ‘lace,’ isn’t there? The very sound of them makes me feel like skipping off to a dance. And yellow silk. It makes one think of a dress of sunshine. I always wanted a yellow silk dress, but first my mother and then my husband wouldn’t hear of it. The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> If you are going to marry a minister, you will have to give up such expressions as ‘dig in.’  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux; but, I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>

> But I mistrust you haven’t any too much sense yet. It’s not to be expected, of course. Experience teaches sense. You can’t learn it in a college course. You’ve been to college four years and I never was, but I know heaps more than you do, young ladies.  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>
